title: Email templates with Mailgen
idea: Mailgen turns a plain JavaScript object into a styled HTML email and a plain-text version, so you never hand-write email HTML.
points: `new Mailgen({ theme, product })` sets the look and the sender's name and link.
A `body` holds `name`, `intro`, an optional `action` button and `outro`.
`generate` returns the HTML; `generatePlaintext` returns the text version.
Wrap each email in a function of the username and a link.

code.caption: Both templates, then a demo. Setting `copyright` keeps the footer fixed; the default footer shows the current year. Step through, then press Run.

walk.text: One `Mailgen` instance sets the look and the product's name, link and footer text.
A template is a function of the username and a link. `name` greets, `intro` opens, `outro` closes.
`action` adds a button: `instructions` above it, then `text`, `link` and `color`.
The password-reset template has the same shape; only the words, color and link change.
Build both emails for `ada`, with fixed demo links.
`generatePlaintext` prints the text. `generate` returns HTML, checked here for each link.

pitfalls: Mailgen does not escape HTML in `name` or `intro`; escape user input first.
Send both versions: `generate` for HTML and `generatePlaintext` for clients that show only text.
Use a full `https://` URL in `button.link`; an email has no base address for relative paths.

quiz.why:
The text version is plain words with no tags. The HTML version wraps each paragraph in `

` tags.

takeaway: Describe the email as data; Mailgen renders the HTML and the text.

starters: How do I add a logo or change the theme?
